s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal pain and distension with a large hepatic mass and vascular complications
salient_findings: Abdominal distension without guarding or rebound
Large mixed solid and cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe
IVC thrombus and near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
key_facts: 8-year-old girl with no significant medical history
1-week history of progressive abdominal pain
Nausea and vomiting
Abdominal distension without guarding or rebound
17 × 9 cm mixed solid and cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe
Compression of the inferior vena cava (IVC)
Percutaneous biopsy of the mass and placement of a drain
Persistent sanguineous output from the drain
Anemia and concern for hemorrhage
Infrarenal IVC thrombus and near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
Compression of the distal IVC at its junction with the right atrium

shortlist.label: Hepatoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large hepatic mass with vascular complications in a pediatric patient

shortlist.label: Embryonal sarcoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive liver tumor with potential for hemorrhage and vascular invasion

shortlist.label: Hepatic angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant liver tumor with high risk of bleeding and vascular complications

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but aggressive liver tumor that can present with abdominal pain and distension

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant liver tumor that can cause abdominal pain, distension, and vascular complications

raw.rationale: The patient's age, lack of significant medical history, and presence of a large mixed solid and cystic mass in the liver are consistent with hepatoblastoma, which is the most common primary liver cancer in children.

rejected.label: Embryonal sarcoma of the liver
rejected.why: While possible, embryonal sarcoma is less common than hepatoblastoma in children and typically presents with more aggressive features.

rejected.label: Hepatic angiosarcoma
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that is more commonly associated with exposure to toxic substances and is unlikely in an 8-year-old girl with no significant medical history.

rejected.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less specific and does not account for the distinct features of the patient's presentation as well as hepatoblastoma does.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: This is the most common type of liver cancer in adults but is rare in children, especially those without underlying liver disease or risk factors.
